title: Binance, BitGet, and the Credential Playbook That Keeps Working
content_md: Tl;DR $6.34 billion in crypto assets affected : On October 29, 2026, Binance suffered an attack the FBI attributed to the DPRK, with attackers moving from compromised engineering workstations to the systems responsible for signing wallet transactions. Binance, BitGet and a third company, one pattern : After initial access, attackers relied on legitimate credentials and permissions to move laterally toward production systems; only the initial access vector changed. 44% of compromised machines held more than 10 secrets : Developer environments are prime targets for credential theft; what limits the blast radius is knowing where your credentials live, what they access, and how quickly you can revoke them. On October 29, 2026, Binance suffered an attack affecting approximately $6.34 billion in crypto assets. The company recently published its initial investigation findings, explaining how the attackers moved from compromised engineering workstations to the systems responsible for signing wallet transactions. The FBI has attributed the attack to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), identifying the activity as TraderTraitor . Since September, at least three cryptocurrency companies have experienced attacks with striking similarities: Binance : Approximately $6.34 billion in assets were affected, with $2.85 billion frozen or intercepted as of November 3.
